name: Neuchâtel
flagName: Flag of the Canton of Neuchâtel
summary: Green, white and red vertical bands with a small white cross in the upper fly. Adopted when Neuchâtel became a republic in 1848.
origin: Neuchâtel joined the Confederacy in 1815 but remained a principality of the King of Prussia until the revolution of 1848, which adopted the green-white-red tricolour.

symbols.name: White cross
symbols.description: A small Swiss cross in the red band.

facts: It was the only Swiss canton that was also a principality of a foreign king.
Italy's flag uses the same colours.
clues: Green, white and red vertical bands with a small white cross.
A canton that was once ruled by the King of Prussia.
